title: Bank of Baroda Hikes 555-Day FD Rate to 6.85 Percent: What Rs 1 Lakh Earns
excerpt: The bob Golden Goal 555-day deposit now pays 6.85% to general customers and up to 7.50% to super senior citizens, effective November 12 — the only tenor the bank changed.
body:
• Bank of Baroda has raised the rate on its 555-day 'bob Golden Goal' deposit by 10 basis points, effective November 12, 2026 — general customers now earn 6.85% on callable deposits and 6.90% on non-callable.
  • Senior citizens earn 7.35% (callable) and super senior citizens, aged 80 and above, up to 7.50% on non-callable deposits. Only this tenor changed; all other rates are unchanged.
  • At 6.85% with quarterly compounding, Rs 1 lakh grows to about Rs 1,10,880 in 555 days, Rs 2 lakh to about Rs 2,21,759 and Rs 5 lakh to about Rs 5,54,399 (calculated from the bank's stated rate; actual payout follows the bank's compounding terms).
  • The scheme covers retail deposits below Rs 3 crore, including NRE and NRO accounts — NRIs holding NRE/NRO deposits are eligible at the general-customer rate.

Bank of Baroda has raised the interest rate on its special 555-day fixed deposit, the bob Golden Goal Deposit Scheme, by 10 basis points, with the revised rates effective November 12, 2026, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. The change applies only to the 555-day tenor — rates on all other tenors remain unchanged — and covers retail term deposits below Rs 3 crore.

The new rates

General customers, including NRE and NRO account holders, now earn 6.85% per annum on callable deposits and 6.90% on non-callable deposits, up from 6.75%. Senior citizens receive 7.35% callable and 7.40% non-callable. Super senior citizens — resident customers aged 80 and above — receive 7.45% callable and a peak 7.50% on non-callable deposits. Executive Director Beena Vaheed said the increase was aimed at offering competitive returns while supporting the bank's deposit franchise and the credit requirements of a growing economy; the bank described the revision as part of its asset-liability management, designed to strengthen its deposit base without compromising margin stability.

What Rs 1 lakh, Rs 2 lakh and Rs 5 lakh earn

At the general-customer callable rate of 6.85%, compounded quarterly over 555 days (about 18 months), Rs 1 lakh grows to approximately Rs 1,10,880 — interest of about Rs 10,880. Rs 2 lakh grows to approximately Rs 2,21,759 (interest about Rs 21,759), and Rs 5 lakh to approximately Rs 5,54,399 (interest about Rs 54,399). At the senior-citizen callable rate of 7.35%, Rs 1 lakh grows to approximately Rs 1,11,711. These are arithmetic calculations from the bank's stated rates, not bank-issued illustrations; the exact maturity value on your deposit will follow the bank's compounding and premature-withdrawal terms, and interest is taxable in India.

Why banks are raising deposit rates now

Bank of Baroda is not moving alone. The revision follows the Reserve Bank of India's 25-basis-point repo rate increase in October 2026, after which HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Overseas Bank and Indian Bank have also raised rates on select tenures, according to banking-sector reporting. Deposit rates do not move uniformly after a policy hike — each bank adjusts the tenors where it needs funding — which is why this change is confined to a single special tenor rather than the whole rate card.

How to open it

Customers can open the deposit through the bank's bob World mobile app, its net banking platform, or at any branch, according to the bank. New-to-bank customers can also open a fixed deposit online through the Bank of Baroda website without first opening a savings account. For NRIs, the scheme's inclusion of NRE and NRO deposits at the general rate is the relevant detail — NRE interest remains repatriable under the usual rules, while NRO interest is taxed at source; check the current terms on the bank's site before booking, since special-tenor schemes can be withdrawn or repriced without a long notice period.
